title: PEB Design Parameters: Span, Height, Load | Steel Mind Engineers
description: The data an engineer needs to design your steel building: width, length, eave height, roof slope, loads, bay spacing and site location.
h1: Basic Parameters: The Data Needed to Design Your Steel Building
quickAnswer: To design a steel building, an engineer needs the width, length, eave height, roof slope, bay spacing, loads, site location, openings and any crane or mezzanine. A rough sketch with these numbers is enough to start.
alt: Diagram showing width, eave height and roof slope of a pre-engineered building.

faq.a: It is the height from the floor to the point where the roof meets the side wall.

faq.q: Can I change the size after the quote?
faq.a: Yes. The price will change with the size, and the engineer will update the quote.

blocks.text: Every design starts with a few numbers. If they are correct, the quote is accurate and the design is fast. If they are wrong, the structure may be too weak or too costly. Collect the items below before you request a quote.

items.name: Width
items.text: The distance between the two side walls, measured from the outside face of one sidewall girt to the outside face of the other. This sets the span of the frame.

items.name: Length
items.text: The distance along the building between the end walls. It is divided into bays.

items.name: Bay spacing
items.text: The distance between two frames. The best spacing depends on the loads and the roof system, and the engineer will confirm it.

items.name: Eave height
items.text: The height from the floor to the top of the outer eave purlin. Set it from the tallest machine, stack or truck that must enter. Clear height, measured to the bottom of the rafter, and ridge height, measured to the peak, are also stated.

items.name: Roof slope
items.text: The angle of the roof. A low slope between 0.5 in 10 and 1.5 in 10 is common for PEB. Rain and sheet type affect the choice.

items.name: Loads
items.text: Include the dead load, the live load, wind, and any special loads such as solar panels, hanging equipment or cranes.

items.name: Location
items.text: The site decides wind speed and rain intensity. Give the city and, if possible, the exact site.

items.name: Openings
items.text: List the number, size and position of doors, windows and loading docks.

items.name: Extras
items.text: Mention any crane, mezzanine, insulation, skylight or future extension.

blocks.title: Framing and Sheeting in the Parameters

blocks.text: Primary framing means the columns and rafters. Secondary framing means the purlins and girts that carry the sheets and brace the main frames. The sheeting is the roof and wall cover, usually hot-dip galvanized, zinc-aluminium coated steel.

blocks.title: If You Do Not Have All the Data

blocks.text: Send what you have. The engineer will ask for the rest. A rough sketch or a photo of the site is enough to begin.
